legend.X: negative/control evidence weakens the proposed bridge

cases.jurisdiction_note: Internationally recognized Ukrainian territory under Russian occupation; historical proof-of-concept, not a sovereign third-country procurement case.
cases.evidence_summary: Russian forces compelled or caused local networks to reroute through Russian-controlled providers such as Miranda Media/Rostelecom-linked infrastructure; users then inherited Russian censorship/surveillance conditions, with restrictions on external services and an explicit information-control objective reported by Ukrainian authorities and independent network observers.

Kazakhstan uses Russian-origin SORM/DPI; Freedom House reports authorities attempted targeted filtering with Russian DPI during the January 2022 protest crisis before escalating to nationwide shutdown. Kazakhtelecom has both Russian and non-Russian international transit, enabling matched-path tests.
cases.blocker: Exact device/vendor lineage and any Russian remote-control involvement remain unresolved.

cases.evidence_summary: Russian-developed SORM has been used since 2010; independent media and information sources are heavily blocked, self-censorship is severe, and state/Kremlin-aligned narratives dominate much of the information environment. A substantial share of internet traffic has historically passed through Russia.
cases.blocker: No device-level evidence in this pass proves Russian SORM itself executes the blocking or is commanded remotely by Russia.

cases.evidence_summary: All ISPs/mobile providers are required to maintain Russian-model SORM compliance; authorities actively block content and TikTok, and international connectivity is concentrated through Kazakhstan and China with Russia a relevant regional transit path in broader routing data.
cases.blocker: No evidence that Russia remotely ordered the observed Kyrgyz blocks.

cases.evidence_summary: Uzbekistan imported Russian SORM/DPI technology and maintains routine website blocking, surveillance, and a history of protest-related internet shutdowns including Karakalpakstan in 2022.
cases.blocker: Specific filtering events are not yet tied to a specific Russian-origin device or external command channel.

cases.evidence_summary: ETECSA is a Russian-technology procurement target in the existing export graph and operates Cuba's state telecom monopoly; Cuba exhibits protest-correlated connectivity disruptions, independent-media blocking and coordinated pro-government manipulation.
cases.blocker: No public evidence in this pass connects a Russian device to the specific blocking events or proves Russian remote control.

cases.evidence_summary: Nicaragua reportedly deployed Russian government-linked SORM-3 around 2018 and deepened cybersecurity cooperation with Russia. Surveillance, intimidation and self-censorship are strongly documented, but broad website blocking was not the dominant 2024 technical pattern.
cases.blocker: No evidence of TSPU-like filtering or Russian remote command.

reverse_ranking.reason: Integrated route-control + Russian censorship + information-control mechanism is directly documented, but occupation changes the legal/operational context.
Best sovereign-country evidence that Russian DPI was actually attempted for targeted filtering during a political crisis.
Strongest sovereign information-capture analog combining Russian surveillance lineage, heavy censorship and pro-Kremlin narrative environment.
Mandatory Russian-model SORM and active platform/media blocking plus useful transit topology.
Russian SORM/DPI imports plus strong censorship record but weaker device-event linkage.
High strategic relevance to the United States and strong information control, but weak Russian-device-to-blocking bridge.
Valuable falsifier: Russian SORM exposure is compatible with surveillance-heavy control without broad TSPU-style blocking.

highest_value_next_checks: Resolve the exact Russian DPI vendor/product used by Kazakhstan during January 2022 targeted-filtering attempts.
Search vendor maintenance architecture, procurement clauses, firmware/update channels and sanctions/forensics for remote administrative access evidence in sovereign deployments.
Build country-specific censorship timelines and compare them for suspicious synchronization only after a normal independent-policy baseline is frozen.
Use Kazakhstan mixed-transit paths as the first route-dependent fingerprint test because Russian and non-Russian upstreams coexist.
Preserve Nicaragua as a permanent negative control against the claim 'Russian SORM export implies mass filtering'.
